sentences.text: The most common way a model fails is not that it learned too little, but that it learned the wrong thing: the noise in its training data.
sentences.say: The most common way a model fails is not that it learned too little, but that it learned the wrong thing: the noise in its training data.

sentences.text: Understanding this failure, and the tools against it, is what separates a working model from a demo that falls apart on real data.
sentences.say: Understanding this failure, and the tools against it, is what separates a working model from a demo that falls apart on real data.

sentences.text: Key ideas
sentences.say: Key ideas

sentences.text: Underfitting (high bias): too simple, bad on training data and on new data.
sentences.say: Underfitting (high bias): too simple, bad on training data and on new data.

sentences.text: Overfitting (high variance): too flexible, great on training data, bad on new data.
sentences.say: Overfitting (high variance): too flexible, great on training data, bad on new data.

sentences.text: The test error is U-shaped as flexibility grows, while the training error only goes down.
sentences.say: The test error is U-shaped as flexibility grows, while the training error only goes down.

sentences.text: The gap between them is the warning sign.
sentences.say: The gap between them is the warning sign.

sentences.text: Regularization adds a penalty on large weights to the cost.
sentences.say: Regularization adds a penalty on large weights to the cost.

sentences.text: It trades a little training accuracy for better behaviour on new data.
sentences.say: It trades a little training accuracy for better behaviour on new data.

sentences.text: The strength is lambda.
sentences.say: The strength is lambda.

sentences.text: The same fourteen noisy points, fitted three ways.

sentences.text: The straight line is too simple: it misses the curve in the data (underfitting).

sentences.text: The gentle curve follows the real pattern.
sentences.say: The gentle curve follows the real pattern.

sentences.text: The wiggly curve passes close to every dot, but between the dots it swings wildly, and it will predict badly for a new input (overfitting).
sentences.say: The wiggly curve passes close to every dot, but between the dots it swings wildly, and it will predict badly for a new input (overfitting).

sentences.text: 11.2 Bias and variance
sentences.say: 11.2 Bias and variance

sentences.text: StatQuest's Bias and Variance video (7 minutes) gives the standard words for the two failures:
sentences.say: StatQuest's Bias and Variance video (7 minutes) gives the standard words for the two failures:

sentences.text: Bias is the systematic miss of a model that is too simple to follow the true pattern.
sentences.say: Bias is the systematic miss of a model that is too simple to follow the true pattern.

sentences.text: A straight line through a curve is wrong in the same way on every dataset.
sentences.say: A straight line through a curve is wrong in the same way on every dataset.

sentences.text: Variance is how much a model changes when you give it a different sample of data.
sentences.say: Variance is how much a model changes when you give it a different sample of data.

sentences.text: A very flexible model fits whatever noise it was shown, so a different sample gives a very different curve.
sentences.say: A very flexible model fits whatever noise it was shown, so a different sample gives a very different curve.

sentences.text: The figure averages 200 runs on data from a wavy curve plus noise.
sentences.say: The figure averages 200 runs on data from a wavy curve plus noise.

sentences.text: The test error is the error on new data.
sentences.say: The test error is the error on new data.

sentences.say: For a straight line (degree 1) it is 0.293, for a cubic (degree 3) it is 0.120, and for a degree 11 polynomial it is 0.372.

sentences.say: A model that scores nearly perfectly on its own training data can be the worst on new data.

sentences.text: This is the bias-variance trade-off: simpler models have more bias and less variance, flexible ones the reverse, and the best model sits in between.
sentences.say: This is the bias-variance trade-off: simpler models have more bias and less variance, flexible ones the reverse, and the best model sits in between.

sentences.text: 11.4 Three remedies for overfitting
sentences.say: 11.4 Three remedies for overfitting

sentences.text: Collect more data.
sentences.say: Collect more data.

sentences.text: With many more examples the wiggly curve cannot pass through all of them.
sentences.say: With many more examples the wiggly curve cannot pass through all of them.

sentences.text: It is the best cure but often impossible.
sentences.say: It is the best cure but often impossible.

sentences.text: Use fewer features (or lower the polynomial degree).
sentences.say: Use fewer features (or lower the polynomial degree).

sentences.text: Pick the most relevant ones; this is called feature selection.

sentences.text: A downside: you throw away information.
sentences.say: A downside: you throw away information.

sentences.text: Regularize.

sentences.text: 11.5 Regularization
sentences.say: 11.5 Regularization

sentences.text: The wiggles of an overfit model come from large weights: the model needs big numbers to bend sharply.
sentences.say: The wiggles of an overfit model come from large weights: the model needs big numbers to bend sharply.

sentences.text: So add a penalty for large weights to the cost, and training has to balance fit against simplicity:
sentences.say: So add a penalty for large weights to the cost, and training has to balance fit against simplicity:

sentences.text: The first term is the usual error: fit the data.
sentences.say: The first term is the usual error: fit the data.

sentences.text: The second is the new penalty: keep the weights small.
sentences.say: The second is the new penalty: keep the weights small.

sentences.text: lambda (a hyperparameter you choose) sets the balance.
sentences.say: lambda (a hyperparameter you choose) sets the balance.

sentences.text: With lambda = 0 there is no penalty, and you are back to the original model.
sentences.say: With lambda equals 0 there is no penalty, and you are back to the original model.

sentences.text: With a huge lambda the weights are pushed to almost zero and the model becomes nearly flat, which underfits.
sentences.say: With a huge lambda the weights are pushed to almost zero and the model becomes nearly flat, which underfits.

sentences.text: The bias b is usually not penalized (Ng, video 39).
sentences.say: The bias b is usually not penalized (Ng, video 39).

sentences.text: Dividing by 2m, as in the first term, keeps lambda comparable across datasets of different size.
sentences.say: Dividing by 2m, as in the first term, keeps lambda comparable across datasets of different size.

sentences.text: In gradient descent the only change is one extra term in the update of each weight (Ng, videos 40 and 41, for linear and logistic regression):
